dosing.evidence: an intraperitoneal injection (i.p.) of psilocybin (10 mg/kg, LGC, CAY-14041). ... All drugs were dissolved in 0.9% NaCl prior to administration.
a single subcutaneous (s.c.) injection of ketamine hydrochloride (10 mg/kg, LGC, MM0144.00-0250)
Fluoxetine hydrochloride (20 mg/kg/day, Sigma-Aldrich, F132) was administered via i.p. injection once daily for 2 consecutive weeks

group_housing.evidence: All C57BL/6J mice were housed in groups of 5-8 per cage

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12/12 hours light/dark cycles, lights on at 7 a.m. ... All testing was conducted at the beginning of the light cycle.

assays.assay_description: Rectangular white plexiglass chamber (42 x 42 x 42 cm). Two consecutive 2.5-min sessions: 'no target' (empty perforated cylinder) followed by 'target' (unfamiliar CD1 mouse in the cylinder). Time in the 4-cm interaction zone around the cylinder was recorded with ANY-maze and used to compute the social preference score. Test repeated pre-treatment (D11) and at 24 h, 7 d, and 14 d post-treatment.

application_type.evidence: ketamine (10 mg/kg, s.c.); psilocybin (10 mg/kg, i.p.); Fluoxetine (20 mg/kg/day, i.p.)

setup_restrain.evidence: The test was performed in dim lighting conditions (30 lx) in rectangular white plexiglass chambers

food_restriction.evidence: food and water available ad libitum [in home cage]; test apparatus is a plexiglass chamber with no food access

water_restriction.evidence: food and water available ad libitum [in home cage]; test apparatus has no water access

time_to_assay.evidence: the mice underwent subsequent SP tests at 24 h, 7- and 14-days post-administration

sample_size.evidence: Table 1: CSD Psilocybin 10 mg/kg, No of Animals: 16, No of Susceptible Animals: 8

outcomes.summary: A single i.p. dose of psilocybin (10 mg/kg) significantly reversed social avoidance in stress-susceptible mice, increasing the social preference score at 24 h, 7 days, and 14 days post-administration. Effects were rapid and sustained, contrasting with fluoxetine which required 14 days of chronic dosing.
outcomes.statistics: p < 0.05 vs. pre-treatment (Mixed-effects ANOVA with Fisher's LSD)
outcomes.evidence: Ketamine and psilocybin each produced rapid and sustained antidepressant-like effects, significantly (p < 0.05) reducing social avoidance behavior at 24 h, 7 days, and 14 days following a single administration.

judge_notes: Single behavioural assay across the study (Social Preference test); all three candidates agreed on this paradigm.
D3 set to '2-7' (4 recording days: D11 baseline + D13 + D19 + D26); GLM's '8-14' appears to be an error counting calendar days rather than recording days for this assay.

B1 scored as '2-3' (time without target, time with target, and derived SP score) per qwen; B4 scored 0 because only spatial zone time was measured (paraphrased per rubric: zone time is not ethological).
Listed all three administered compounds in the dosing block (psilocybin, ketamine, fluoxetine) per rubric instruction to capture every compound administered.
Housing handling and enrichment marked 'not_reported' — paper does not mention either.
time_to_assay set to 'multiple' (24 h, 7 d, 14 d post-dose) with value_minutes anchored to first post-treatment session (1440 min).
